name: S20 -> g193_budget_floor B1b: core injection is skipped on every INJURED cell, deleting core sections on days the run does not own
why: B1b is the only assertion in this gate that can see it. B1a is HEALTHY-ONLY by construction (O1: the 18-per-build hand count does not extend to the injury paths), so a deletion confined to shoulder/lowback/elbox protect scores 18/18 on every healthy cell and passes B1a clean. The deletion lands overwhelmingly on ordinary lift days, NOT on NRC long-run tier days, so it is exactly the class of loss the D46 carve-out must NOT swallow: if the carve-out had been written too wide this mutation would survive. Measured against the transcribed V192 off-long-run census (no baseline file: the sabotage runner never supplies one), shoulder/protect 648 -> 0, lowback/protect 1224 -> 0, elbow/protect 576 -> 0.
anchor: if(includeCore && !inTaper(w) && !isRecoveryWeek(w)) injectDynamicCore(weeks[w], dayRoles, trainDays, w, cfg.equipment||'home_full');
replacement: if(includeCore && !inTaper(w) && !isRecoveryWeek(w) && !(cfg.injury && cfg.injury.region)) injectDynamicCore(weeks[w], dayRoles, trainDays, w, cfg.equipment||'home_full');

name: S21 -> g193_budget_floor B1b: _longRunTier claims every day is a long run, so the carve-out swallows the whole assertion
why: The carve-out is only as honest as the predicate behind it. B1b excludes days the engine's own _longRunTier calls a long-run tier, and reads that predicate out of the file under test rather than keeping a second private copy — which means widening the predicate is a way to make B1b vacuous without touching B1b. This mutation does exactly that: every day classifies as tier B, the excluded set becomes 28224/28224 day-builds, and every off-long-run core count falls to zero against the transcribed V192 census. B1b names it. Recorded deliberately: this is the mutation that proves the carve-out cannot be widened silently, which is the new risk this amendment introduced.
